llm.summary: This browser automation skill is openly high-powered, but it needs review because it can save and restore logged-in sessions and move files without built-in per-action safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The skill repeatedly frames use as trusted, local, visible browser automation and mitigates the daemon with localhost binding, a random token, non-headless Chrome, safe mode for eval/run-code, and idle auto-exit. Those mitigations are useful, but the tool remains inappropriate for untrusted agents or public service exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package metadata and lockfile show a simple Node package depending on playwright-core, with no hidden install script or bundled node_modules. Browser use starts through explicit daemon/client commands rather than install-time execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions expose first-class cookie and localStorage list/export/import/set/clear commands plus upload/download and raw code paths. These are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but they give an agent broad session and file-transfer authority with no enforced per-operation confirmation or path allowlist.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon intentionally persists browser state across commands, writes its token state under ~/.pw-browser, and can export/import cookies and localStorage to caller-chosen files. Exported session files are correctly documented as secrets, but the code does not enforce restricted storage, expiry, encryption, or safe-mode blocking for those session operations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Playwright browser automation, and the artifacts clearly disclose powerful capabilities including page JavaScript eval, sandboxed Playwright run-code, credentialed browser requests, cookie/localStorage management, upload, download, screenshots, and persistent browser state.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a trusted local environment where you are comfortable letting an agent control a visible browser session. Treat exported cookies and localStorage as passwords: avoid exporting by default, keep any files in a restricted directory, delete them promptly, and do not let untrusted prompts or agents call this skill against logged-in accounts.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Verified: pw-browser.js implements cookie and localStorage list/export/import/clear/set operations. This is coherent with advanced browser automation and is disclosed in SKILL.md and README.en.md, but it materially increases session-token handling risk.
[SDI-1] expected: Verified: upload uses Playwright setInputFiles and download uses download.saveAs. File transfer is a normal browser automation capability and is documented, though it can move arbitrary caller-specified local files or save remote content without built-in path restrictions.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Verified: cookie/storage export and import directly read or write caller-selected JSON paths. The session-management feature is documented, but the lack of enforced confirmation, restricted directory, or protection for exported secrets supports the Review bucket.
[RA2] expected: Verified: README.en.md and SKILL.md explicitly describe session backup/restore and warn that exported files can impersonate the user. This transparency prevents a malicious verdict, but the persistence capability remains high impact.
[TM1] expected: Verified: the skill combines persistent daemon-held browser state, cookie/storage import/export, local file writes, eval, and run-code. The artifacts disclose these capabilities and limit eval/run-code with safe mode, but safe mode does not block cookie/storage read-write, so installation should be reviewed carefully.
